The gum obtained from Sterculia urens and other species of Sterculia. Irregular or vermiform pieces, grey- ish-white with a brown or pink tinge, with an odour resembling that of acetic acid. It contains not less than 14.0% of volatile acid (or not less than 10.0% if supplied in powdered form), calculated as acetic acid. Sparingly soluble in water, but swells into a homo- geneous, adhesive, gelatinous mass; practically insoluble in alco- hol. Store at a temperature not exceeding 25°. Adverse Effects and Precautions As for Ispaghula, p.1737. There is a risk of intestinal or oesopha- geal obstruction and faecal impaction, especially if such com- pounds are swallowed dry. Therefore they should always be tak- en with sufficient fluid and should not be taken immediately before going to bed. They should be avoided by patients who have difficulty swallowing.
